messages:
OpsBot: INCIDENT ALERT — High 5xx/403 spike on canary authz-service. Detector: routing/ingress telemetry. Affected perf: increased latency, failed requests to /v1/authorize. Pager sent to @eng-oncall.
Cara Wu: seeing it on the dashboard. canary (canary-a) error rate ~28% 5xx, production baseline ~0.4%.
Sanjay Patel: @Cara any recent deploys? I triggered a small kernel/quant change earlier but that was model runtime. Not authz.
Dylan Reed: I pushed a routing policy change 12m ago to experiment with weighted split for authz canaries — verifying now.
Marta Gomez: @Dylan can you confirm weight? Canary was supposed to be 1% but metrics show 30%.
Dylan Reed: ack — I see a stale annotation in the ingress that set weight: 30. It should have been 1. Looks like the rollout script didn't pick up the override.
Cara Wu: ok kill-switch plan: flip ff_authz_v2 to false (kills new authz path) and rollback the routing override. Doing quick impact check for any dependent services.
Sanjay Patel: agree. Quick commands:
```
# check canary traffic distribution
kubectl -n infra get svc authz-proxy -o yaml | grep traffic-weight -A2
# tail errors
kubectl -n prod logs -l app=authz-proxy -c main --since=10m | grep 5.. | head
```
Cara Wu: flipped feature flag ff_authz_v2 -> false via admin console. Confirmed change at 1717567998.
OpsBot: SYSTEM: Feature flag change detected: ff_authz_v2 changed to false by Cara Wu.
Sanjay Patel: rolling back ingress annotation now. Command: `kubectl patch ingress authz -n prod --type=json -p '[{"op":"replace","path":"/metadata/annotations/edge\.redwood\.io~1traffic-weight","value":"1"}]'`
Dylan Reed: rollback applied 1717568086. Observing metrics.
Marta Gomez: downstream 403s dropped sharply, 200s increased. Latency back to baseline ~120ms.
Lucas Kim: customer support ticket spike: a handful of customers saw 401 during 5m window. SupportBot: routing IDs: C-472, C-489 flagged.
SupportBot: Notified CS reps, they are triaging, will reach out if customers want post-incident notes.
Cara Wu: summary so far: root cause — rollout script left a stale ingress override; canary received ~30% traffic; authz-v2 path had tighter failure handling leading to errors. Kill-switch + rollback mitigated.
Dylan Reed: long-term fix items: validation in rollout script to fail if weight != expected; alert rule for canary traffic drift; add canary pre-checks.
Sanjay Patel: creating an incident ticket and will assign postmortem. Quick follow-ups: (1) revert the temporary runtime change if needed (it wasn't the cause but worth auditing), (2) add an automated check to detect FF flips with large traffic change, (3) CS customer outreach template.
OpsBot: PAGING: Handoff to next on-call in 30m. Current on-call: Cara Wu. Next on-call: Marta Gomez.
Marta Gomez: I will take the handoff at 1717569123. Leaving a note: watch authz error budget and customer tickets for 2h.
Cara Wu: leaving handoff context: reverted routing override, ff_authz_v2 disabled, observed 5xx -> baseline. Logs and the rollout script revision: `git rev-parse HEAD` = `a3f2d7b`. I attached the command output to the incident ticket.
Dylan Reed: adding a quick mitigations doc snippet to ticket: steps to revert and verification queries.
Lucas Kim: CS flagged 2 customers with higher impact— offering SLO credit option. Keep me posted if anything else pops.
SupportBot: CS updates queued.
Cara Wu: final note before handoff: runbook step 4 (validate ingress annotations) was missed — updating runbook now. Postmortem required.
Marta Gomez: acknowledged. I'll own the postmortem write-up and schedule a blameless review.
Dylan Reed: thanks all — closing active mitigation. Monitoring on for 2 hours.
OpsBot: INCIDENT RESOLVED status: mitigation confirmed; monitor period started.
